'''Steven Alan Orszag''' (February 27, 1943 – May 1, 2011) was an American mathematician.

==Life and career==
Orszag was born to a [[American Jews|Jewish]] family in [[Manhattan]], the son of Joseph Orszag, a lawyer.<ref name=StAndrews>[http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/history/Biographies/Orszag.html University of St Andrews, Scotland - School of Mathematics and Statistics: "Steven Alan Orszag" by J.J. O'Connor and E.F. Robertson] October 2011</ref> Orszag's paternal grandparents were emigrants from [[Hungarian Jews|Hungary]].<ref name=StAndrews /> Orszag was raised in [[Forest Hills, Queens]] and graduated from [[Forest Hills High School (New York)|Forest Hills High School]].<ref name=StAndrews /> In 1962, at the age of 19, he graduated with a B.S. in Mathematics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]<ref name=StAndrews /> where he was a member of the [[Pi Lambda Phi]] fraternity.<ref>2011 Pi Lambda Phi Membership Directory</ref> He did post graduate study at [[Cambridge University]] and in 1966 graduated with a Ph.D. in [[astrophysics]] from [[Princeton University]].<ref name=StAndrews /> His thesis adviser was [[Martin David Kruskal]].<ref name=StAndrews /> In 1967, Orszag was appointed as a professor of applied mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he collaborated with [[Carl M. Bender]],<ref name=StAndrews /> and was a Member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name=IAS>[https://www.ias.edu/scholars/steven-orszag Institute for Advanced Study profile]</ref> In 1984, he was appointed Forrest E Hamrick Professor of Engineering at [[Princeton University]]. In 1998, he accepted a position at [[Yale University]] and in 2000,<ref name=StAndrews /> he was named the Percey F. Smith [[Professor of Mathematics]] at [[Yale University]]<ref>{{cite web  |url=http://www.yale.edu/opa/arc-ybc/v29.n10/story7.html  |title=Steven Orszag appointed the new Percey F. Smith Professor of Mathematics  |access-date=2008-11-27 |date=November 10, 2000 |work=Yale Bulletin & Calendar, Volume 29, Number 10  |publisher=[[Yale University]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090418121152/http://www.yale.edu/opa/arc-ybc/v29.n10/story7.html |archive-date=April 18, 2009 |quote=Orszag is the coauthor or coeditor of nine books, including "Studies in Applied Mathematics," "Numerical Analysis of Spectral Methods," "Advanced Mathematical Methods for Scientists and Engineers," "Supercomputers and Fluid Dynamics," "Japanese Supercomputing: Architecture, Algorithms, and Applications," and "Large Eddy Simulation of Complex Engineering and Geophysical Flows." His latest book, "Partial Differential Equations for Scientists and Engineers," a collaboration with C.M. Bender, is forthcoming.}}</ref> from 2000 until his death in 2011.<ref name = BulletinObit/>

Orszag has won numerous awards including [[Sloan Fellowship]] and [[Guggenheim Fellowship]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gf.org/ofellow.html |title=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation O Fellows Page |access-date=2008-11-27 |publisher=Guggenheim Foundation |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080922092302/http://www.gf.org/ofellow.html |archive-date=September 22, 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]]  Fluid and Plasmadynamics Award, the [[Otto Laporte Award]] of the [[American Physical Society]], and the Society of Engineering Science's G. I. Taylor Medal.<ref>{{cite web  |url=http://www.sesinc.org/medals/prager_taylor.html  |title=William Prager Medal in Solid Mechanics G. I. Taylor Medal in Fluid Mechanics  |access-date=2008-11-27 |publisher=Society of Engineering Science |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080602004812/http://sesinc.org/medals/prager_taylor.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 2008-06-02 |quote=Each award consists of a medal bearing the likeness of the person for whom the award is named and a monetary award of $2000. Recipients will give an address at the annual meeting of the Society...The G. I. Taylor Medal is awarded for outstanding research contributions in either theoretical or experimental Fluid Mechanics or both.  The recipients need not be members of the Society, but become a lifetime members upon receipt of the medals.}}
</ref>

Orszag specialized in [[fluid dynamics]], especially turbulence, [[computational physics]] and mathematics, electronic chip manufacturing, [[Computer data storage|computer storage system]] design, and other topics in [[scientific computing]]. His work included the development of [[spectral methods]], [[pseudo-spectral method]]s, [[direct numerical simulation]]s, renormalization group methods for turbulence, and very-[[large-eddy simulation]]s. He was the founder of and/or chief scientific adviser to a number of companies, including Flow Research, Ibrix (now part of HPQ), Vector Technologies, and Exa Corp. He has been awarded 6 patents and has written over 400 archival papers.{{citation needed|date=October 2015}}

With [[Carl M. Bender]] he wrote [https://www.amazon.com/Advanced-Mathematical-Methods-Scientists-Engineers/dp/0387989315 ''Advanced Mathematical Methods for Scientists and Engineers: Asymptotic Methods and Perturbation Theory''], a standard text on [[Mathematical methods in electronics|mathematical methods]] for scientists.<ref>{{cite web  |url=http://www.maths.leeds.ac.uk/Applied/news.dir/issue20.dir/art/art.html  |title=Advanced Mathematical Methods for Scientists and Engineers: Asymptotic Methods and Perturbation Theory  |access-date=2009-04-18 |first=John |last=Billingham |author-link=<!-- John Billingham not the SETI chap --> |work=UK Nonlinear News, Issue Twenty |publisher=[[University of Leeds]] Department of Applied Mathematics  |date=May 2000  |quote=...the classic book, first published in 1978, on asymptotic methods for ordinary differential equations, difference equations and integrals by Bender and Orszag.}} Book review.</ref><ref>{{cite book  |first=J. P. |last=Goedbloed |author-link=<!-- J. P. Goedbloed --> |author2=Stefaan Poedts  |page=348  |title=Principles of magnetohydrodynamics |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FvM6rMJob-cC&q=Orszag+Bender+(classic+OR+standard)+-site:amazon.com&pg=PA348 |access-date=2009-04-18 |edition=illustrated |year=2004 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-62607-1 |quote=...classical texts ... e.g. Bender and Orszag ... on linear differential equations ... }}</ref> Orszag has been listed as an ISI Highly Cited Author in Engineering by the [[ISI Web of Knowledge]], Thomson Scientific Company.<ref>[http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi?&link1=Browse&link2=Results&id=544 ISI Highly Cited Author - Steven Orszag] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060518071415/http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi?&link1=Browse&link2=Results&id=544 |date=2006-05-18 }}</ref>

===Personal life===
In 1964, he married Reba Karp (sister of [[Joel Karp]],<ref name=StAndrews /> the co-designer of the [[Intel 1103]] chip);<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=ZhoP0KRkQe4C&dq=joel+karp+intel&pg=PA229 PC Magazine: "The First 1024 (1K) Dynamic RAM: The 1103] March 6, 1984</ref> they had three sons: Michael, [[Peter R. Orszag|Peter]], and [[Jonathan Orszag|Jonathan]].<ref name=StAndrews /> Peter and Jonathan were both [[Marshall Scholarship|Marshall Scholars]].<ref>http://www.peterorszag.com and http://www.jonorszag.com</ref>
